arguments.summary: The bug was in `src/textkit/stats.py`, where `word_count` used `len(text.split(" "))`, splitting only on the single ASCII space character. This caused empty strings to count as 1, multiple consecutive spaces to be miscounted, and tabs/newlines/Unicode whitespace (U+00A0, U+3000) to never act as separators. I changed the implementation to `len(text.split())`, which splits on maximal runs of any whitespace character (as defined by `str.isspace()`), treats runs of whitespace as a single separator, and correctly returns 0 for empty or whitespace-only text. Punctuation remains part of adjacent words, and the existing signature is preserved. All 4 pre-existing tests in `tests/test_stats.py` pass, and the full test suite (65 tests) passes, including the whitespace-separator acceptance behavior.
